title: Beef Barley Soup
subtitle: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone
description: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Pat the beef dry and season with half the salt and all the pepper. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the beef in 2 or 3 batches, about 4 minutes each, without crowding the pot so it sears instead of steaming. Move it to a bowl.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.instruction: Lower the heat to medium. Dice the onions and add them to the pot with the carrots and celery. Cook 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the edges soften.

steps.title: Simmer the beef
steps.instruction: Return the beef and its juices to the pot. Add the broth, thyme, and bay leaves, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.

steps.title: Add the barley
steps.instruction: Rinse the barley and stir it in. Simmer partly covered 30–45 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch on the bottom, until the beef is fork-tender and the barley is soft. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.instruction: Remove the bay leaves and skim any fat from the surface. Taste and add the remaining salt. For late calls, keep it covered on low at 140°F or above; it thickens as it sits, so loosen with broth or water before serving.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Beef Barley Soup on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cold-night bowl that fills everyone. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon. Substitute rice or a gluten-free grain.
